title: Peripheral docs contract
lede: Create a register reference in your browser from a register description and optional memory map, component manifest and RTL module. Optional module headers are retained in JSON metadata. Nothing is uploaded, and the published address map is never changed.

sections.title: What you supply
paragraphs: Only the register description is required. Optional inputs add context to the page or portable JSON.
Use UTF-8 files up to 1 MiB each. Generated JSON also stays within 1 MiB so it can be reopened by the tool.

rows: Layout name, software contract ID, registers, offsets, access, fields
Memory map (TOML) or a published base-map region
Region base address and reserved size; adds an address column
Component name, top module, software contract ID, register_bytes
RTL file (.sv) and a module name
The // comment block directly above that module, copied as text

sections.title: Write the register description
paragraphs: Use Prism's register schema. Either your full component manifest or the reduced SDK form below works: name, [interfaces] software and [[registers]], without RTL paths.

The tool checks the same rules as Prism's registers.py load(). Registers are 32-bit words at increasing, 4-byte-aligned offsets. Access is ro, rw or wo; a write-one-to-clear register is rw. The schema has no reset-value or side-effect keys: describe that behavior in the module header.
bullets: Names are lowercase identifiers ([a-z][a-z0-9_]*) and not C/C++ keywords.
Each field has exactly lsb (0-31) and width (1 to 32 - lsb). Fields in one register do not overlap.
A retired standalone *.registers.toml (schema_version, name, contract) is still read, with a notice. The tool never writes that form.
When register_bytes is present, the register description must fit inside that register window.

code.label: uart.toml, reduced SDK form (excerpt: first three registers)
code.text:
name = "uart"

[interfaces]
software = "prism_uart_registers_v1"

[[registers]]
name = "tx"
offset = 0
access = "wo"

[[registers]]
name = "rx"
offset = 4
access = "ro"

[[registers]]
name = "status"
offset = 8
access = "rw"
[registers.fields]
tx_ready = { lsb = 0, width = 1 }
rx_valid = { lsb = 1, width = 1 }
overrun = { lsb = 2, width = 1 }
frame_error = { lsb = 3, width = 1 }

sections.title: Write the module header
paragraphs: The optional comment block directly above your module is copied exactly into JSON metadata and never interpreted. It is not rendered as a duplicate section on peripheral pages. Prism's uart.sv is the model.
Select the RTL file and name the module. The tool offers the component manifest's top module, but never picks one for you.
bullets: Start with a sentence or two on the peripheral's role, then a blank // line.
Add a fixed-width table with the columns Offset, Name, Access and Fields and side effects. Use hex offsets, uppercase names, RO, WO, RW or RO/W1C, and fields such as [7:0] NAME or [1] NAME (W1C).
Finish with a blank // line and notes on aliases, byte lanes, errors and reset.
Put the block on the lines directly above the module keyword, with no blank line between.

code.label: source/soc/peripherals/rtl/uart.sv (excerpt)

sections.title: Which comments are copied
paragraphs: The header is the run of // lines ending on the line directly above the selected module keyword. The tool removes the // and one following space from each line and keeps the rest, including alignment. Comment markers or the word module inside strings and comments never count as code.

rows: // block directly above the selected module
// block separated from the module by a blank line
No; the page shows a notice
No; not supported in this version, with a notice
Never; copying stops at the directive
File or licence header above the `include lines
Comments on other modules in the same file

sections.title: What the tool generates
paragraphs: Every fact in the register table comes from your TOML. Names and access appear exactly as written, so a register your header calls RO/W1C still shows rw. Optional module headers remain in JSON metadata; the tool does not reconcile them with the TOML.

A region is an address reservation, not proof that a device is installed. The UART reserves 4 KiB at 0x40020000 but the SoC decoder routes only its 24-byte register window (register_bytes) to the component.
bullets: Identity: title, layout name, software contract ID, component and top module.
Optional module header, file name, module name and line range retained in JSON metadata.
Register table: hex offset, address (base + offset) when a region is selected, name, access, fields with bit range and mask, and rows for gaps between registers.
Notices and source files with SHA-256 hashes. No local paths or timestamps.
Never added: reset values, side effects, access sequences or interrupt assignments.

sections.title: Errors and notices
paragraphs: An error stops generation and names the file and reason. A notice keeps the page and explains what is missing. Leaving out an optional input removes its context without a notice.

rows: Invalid TOML or register rule failure
Component and register software contract IDs differ
Module name missing, not found or declared twice
Last register past the selected region
No // header directly above the module
Last register past the component's register_bytes

sections.title: Share the result
paragraphs: Download a standalone HTML page, styled like this website, with no scripts or external resources. Also download a JSON file (schema prism-peripheral-doc-v1) that the tool can open again. The same inputs always produce the same files.
Your page is separate from this website. To change Prism or the published address map, contribute to Prism itself.
